full_judgment: 10. It has been noted in many cases that there is a great difference between the expressions "will be dismissed" and "will stand dismissed" as used by the Court in making certain conditional orders. It is clear that the latter expression bears words of finality which do not require any further order from the Court to bring the litigation to a termination. The clear import of such words is that if the amount of money directed to be paid in the said order is paid within the time prescribed, the decree allowing the appeal will stand but if the amount so directed be not paid within the time so fixed the appeal will stand automatically dismissed. On the expiry of the period fixed in the said order, the appeal is brought to a close and completely disposed of and the Court which made the order loses all jurisdiction therein except its power under section 152 of the Code or of review. The Dacca High Court considered similar question in the cases of Manindra Chandra Dey and others Vs. Govinda Prasad (1951) 3 DLR 313 and Sheikh Ayezuddin Vs. Priya Shankar Chowdhury (1954) 6 DLR 505 and the Supreme Court of Pakistan considered this question in Shah Wali Vs. Ghulam Din @ Gamon and Muhammad Din (1967) 19 DLR (SC) 143. The Pakistan Supreme Court case arose out of a suit for pre-emption where a decree was made directing the deposit of a certain sum of money on account of preemption by a certain date with a direction that in default of such deposit the suit would stand dismissed with cost and on appeal the pre-emption money was enhanced with a direction that the amount so enhanced would be deposited within one month of the appellate decree "otherwise the suit will be treated as dismissed with costs". It has been held in the said case that for the Respondent's default in making payment of the correct amount within the time fixed by the appellate decree the suit would stand dismissed and there was no question of extension of time involved either by the original Court or by the appellate Court thereafter, the appeal or revision from the appellate decree having already been dismissed.
